subChunks.title: Conditional Logic — CASE WHEN THEN ELSE END
subChunks.hookHtml: SQL is declarative, but sometimes you need if-else logic inside a query. CASE WHEN is SQL's in-line conditional expression.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Searched CASE

SELECT name, xp,
  CASE
    WHEN xp >= 6500 THEN 'High'
    WHEN xp >= 2000 THEN 'Mid'
    ELSE 'Low'
  END AS xp_tier
FROM apprentices;

Conditions are evaluated top-to-bottom. The first matching WHEN wins. ELSE is the fallback; if omitted and no WHEN matches, the result is NULL.

Simple CASE (equality comparison)

SELECT name,
  CASE rank
    WHEN 'Novice'     THEN 1
    WHEN 'Apprentice' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Adept'      THEN 3
    ELSE 0
  END AS rank_order
FROM apprentices;

CASE in ORDER BY

SELECT name, rank
FROM apprentices
ORDER BY
  CASE rank
    WHEN 'Novice'     THEN 1
    WHEN 'Apprentice' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Adept'      THEN 3
    WHEN 'Mage'       THEN 4
    WHEN 'Archmage'   THEN 5
    ELSE 6
  END;

CASE in aggregate

-- Count apprentices in each XP band:
SELECT
  COUNT(CASE WHEN xp < 1000 THEN 1 END) AS low,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN xp BETWEEN 1000 AND 3000 THEN 1 END) AS mid,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN xp > 3000 THEN 1 END) AS high
FROM apprentices;

storyBeats.text: The sorting ledger needs ranks in logical order, not alphabetical. CASE gives you the sort key.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: CASE WHEN is SQL's if-else. Each WHEN is a condition; the first match wins. ELSE catches everything else. Use it in SELECT to add computed columns, in ORDER BY to define custom sort orders, or inside COUNT to pivot rows into columns.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🪄 XP tier label

Return name, xp, and a computed column tier: 'High' if xp >= 4000, 'Mid' if xp >= 1000, 'Low' otherwise.
subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode:
SELECT name, xp,
  CASE
    WHEN xp >= 4000 THEN 'High'
    WHEN xp >= 1000 THEN 'Mid'
    ELSE 'Low'
  END AS tier
FROM apprentices
ORDER BY xp DESC;

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml:
🏹 Solo

Using CASE inside COUNT, return three columns in one row: low (xp < 1000), mid (xp 1000-3999), high (xp >= 4000). Count of apprentices in each band.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain how CASE WHEN works in SQL, and give an example of using it inside an aggregate function to pivot row data into columns.

questions.prompt: In a CASE expression with multiple WHEN clauses, which condition is applied?
options: The first WHEN that evaluates to true — subsequent WHENs are not evaluated
All matching WHENs are applied in order
All WHENs are evaluated and their results combined
questions.answer: The first WHEN that evaluates to true — subsequent WHENs are not evaluated
questions.explanation: CASE is short-circuit: the first matching WHEN wins and evaluation stops. Order your WHENs from most specific to most general.

questions.prompt: What does a CASE expression return when no WHEN matches and there is no ELSE?
questions.explanation: If no WHEN condition matches and there is no ELSE clause, CASE returns NULL. Always include ELSE to avoid unexpected NULLs in your result.

questions.prompt: How does `COUNT(CASE WHEN xp > 1000 THEN 1 END)` work?
options: Counts rows where xp > 1000 — CASE returns 1 for matching rows and NULL for others; COUNT ignores NULLs
Counts all rows and divides by 1000
Returns 1 if any row has xp > 1000
Throws an error — COUNT requires a column name
questions.answer: Counts rows where xp > 1000 — CASE returns 1 for matching rows and NULL for others; COUNT ignores NULLs
questions.explanation: CASE returns 1 for rows where the condition is true, and NULL for rows where it is false (no ELSE). COUNT(col) ignores NULLs, so it effectively counts only the rows where the condition was true.

questions.prompt: A developer writes ORDER BY rank which sorts ranks alphabetically. Why is that wrong for a rank hierarchy?
options: Alphabetical order does not match the logical rank hierarchy — 'Adept' comes before 'Archmage' alphabetically but not in game logic
ORDER BY cannot be used with text columns
Rank is a reserved word and cannot be used in ORDER BY
SQL always sorts text in ascending order regardless
questions.answer: Alphabetical order does not match the logical rank hierarchy — 'Adept' comes before 'Archmage' alphabetically but not in game logic
questions.explanation: Use CASE in ORDER BY to define a custom sort sequence based on business logic, not alphabetical order.
